Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — PersonaCodeBench, a benchmark that turns user personas into verifiable evolved requirements disclosed progressively in simulated multi-turn coding sessions (controller, user simulator, online requirement evaluator, completion and personalization verifiers); leaderboard of 28 model/effort configurations on the 100-pair Lite release, persona analysis, disclosure ablations and reliability audits

No SDD approach. Evaluated: 28 model/reasoning-effort configurations, e.g. Gemini 4 Argon (medium, high), Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 (medium, high), Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol (medium, high, xhigh), GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Astra (medium, high, xhigh, max), GPT-5.6 Terra, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.7, Grok 4.6, DeepSeek V4.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, Qwen 3.8 27B, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3 Flash, Kimi-K3 (mixed settings); each source's own agent scaffold retained (scaffolds not named per configuration); Harbor 0.23.0 with Docker; GPT-6 Luna (medium) as user simulator and judge

Evaluation workflow: (1) preparation and opening (frozen binding, environment, opening request, possibly with initial-intent blurring); (2) agent work, evidence and online requirement evaluation; (3) feedback and controlled progression (Unmet obligations get feedback, satisfied ones allow disclosure of the next requirement); (4) final verification (completion verifier and personalization verifier). Construction: collection, persona adaptation and fit, contrastive screening, release

Tasks: 100 Lite task-persona pairs. Configurations: 28 model/effort settings; time-budget ladder (max effort at 1x, 2x, 3x) for some models. Baseline: ablations without persona (native-only with neutral simulated user) and with all requirements at opening, for GPT-6 Luna only. Held constant: task-persona assignments, source-specific scaffold, simulator and grading configuration (GPT-6 Luna medium), declared budget policy, Harbor 0.23.0. Acceptance tests: native verifiers plus personalization verifier. Repetitions: repetitions not reported (Section 3.1 says repetitions 'must be frozen' but gives no number; whole-number percentages over 100 tasks and the 26 x 99 run-task records of App. D.3 suggest one run per configuration); the ablation is explicitly single-run. Human intervention: none (simulated user)

GPT-6 Astra max highest Joint pass (48%), then GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh (42%), Claude Opus 5.5 medium (40%), Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 high (39%); best Terminal-bench 3 only 17.4% (4/23); leaders differ by source. Removing persona requirements raises GPT-6 Luna Joint pass from 19% to 45% and completion from 24% to 45%; giving all requirements upfront changes Joint pass only 19% to 20%. Higher effort does not consistently increase conditional pass rates; paired sign tests on 33 within-model setting pairs: only GPT-5.6 Terra high-to-xhigh p = 0.049, none significant after Bonferroni

Distinguished configurations (1% to 48% Joint pass) and separated completion from personalization outcomes (20.5% of native passes fail persona criteria). Repetitions not reported (apparently a single run per configuration; ablation explicitly single-run). Limitations stated: fixed-denominator scoring mixes task performance with evaluation coverage (errors and unexecuted tasks count as zero); SWE-Together has only 4 tasks; persona comparisons descriptive with small groups; conditional rates subject to selection; LLM judge accuracy only moderately aligned with experts; personalization is an operational proxy, not human satisfaction

Limitations: personalization measured as explicit-requirement fulfilment, not human satisfaction; simulator and judge behaviour not fully validated with humans; uneven safeguards across source profiles; proportional sampling does not remove upstream selection effects; small persona groups. Gaps / next steps: complete the study comparing task completion, personalization and interaction effort; validate simulator and judge with human review; broaden task-level control coverage

GPT-6 Luna is at once the contrastive-screening reference agent (tasks kept where it passes natively but fails with persona), the user simulator, the judge and an evaluated model (19% Joint pass), a possible selection bias not discussed (p. 6-7).
